1.title: Will It Tip?
1.topic: two friends build a tall block tower at school and it tips over (school, play, friendship)
lines: *Kim* and *Sid* | *sit* on the *rug*.
Kim has a *big* block. | Sid has a *pink* block.
*Up*, | *up*, | *up* | it *goes*!
It is *big*. | It is *big*! | Will it *tip*? ↗
It *tips*! | It *tips*! | *Bam*! ↘
Kim and Sid *grin*. | Let's *fix* it! ↘
sounds: sit, big, pink, tip, grin, fix
입을 살짝만 벌리고 짧게 '이'. 길게 '이-' 하고 늘이지 마요.
pink는 끝의 k를 짧게 끊고, fix는 '픽스'처럼 ks를 붙여 한 번에.
질문은 끝을 올리고, Bam!은 크게 내려요.
1.expression: Stack the blocks slowly, get excited on “Up, up, up,” hold your breath on “Will it tip?”, shout “Bam!”, then finish with a happy grin.

2.title: Hello, Grandma!
2.topic: a girl video-calls her grandma in Korea and shows her a family drawing (family, feelings, culture)
lines: On Saturday morning, | Mina's tablet *buzzed*.
It was *Grandma*, | calling all the way from *Korea*!
Mina *waved* | and *shouted*, | “*Hi*, Grandma!”
Grandma *smiled*. | “What did you *do* today?” ↘
Mina *picked* up her *drawing*. | “*Look*, Grandma!”
“I *painted* us!” | Grandma *laughed* and *clapped*.
“I *miss* you,” | said Mina. | “I miss you *too*!” ↘
Then they blew a *big* *kiss* | through the *screen*. ↘
sounds: z, v, l 뒤 -ed는 d 소리: waved '웨이브드'처럼 짧게.
k, f, p 뒤 -ed는 짧은 t: laughed '래프트'.
t 뒤 -ed만 '이드'로 한 박자 더: PAINT-ed.
2.expression: Sound surprised when the tablet buzzes, proud when Mina shows her drawing, and soft and warm on “I miss you.”

3.title: Dear Mr. Lopez
3.topic: a thank-you letter to the school crossing guard (community, school, kindness)
lines: *Dear* Mr. Lopez, | my name is Ava, | and I am in *second* grade.
Every morning, | you *help* us cross | the *busy* street | by our school.
You hold up your *bright* red sign, | and all the cars *stop*. ↘
Even on *rainy* days, | you are *always* there | in your yellow *raincoat*.
You know *everyone's* name | and say, “Have a *great* day!”
Last week, | I *dropped* my lunch box | in the middle of the *crosswalk*.
You *picked* it up for me | and walked me *safely* | to the other *side*.
My little brother thinks | you are a *superhero*, | and I *agree*!
Thank you | for keeping us *safe* | every *single* day.
Your *friend*, | Ava ↘
sounds: 말하듯 따뜻하게. 인사 뒤에서 잠깐 쉬어요.
입술을 동그랗게, 혀는 어디에도 닿지 않게.
3.expression: Talk to Mr. Lopez warmly and politely, sound worried in the lunch-box part, and proud on “superhero.”

4.title: Why Geese Fly in a V
4.topic: why Canada geese fly in a V shape when they migrate (animals, science, seasons)
lines: Have you ever *heard* loud honking | high in the autumn *sky*? ↗
Look *up*, | and you may see a flock of *Canada geese* | flying in the shape of a giant *V*.
Every fall, | these birds *migrate*, | or travel *south*, | to find warmer weather and more *food*.
Some flocks fly *thousands* of miles, | and the V shape helps them | make the long *journey*.
When a goose *flaps* its wings, | it stirs up the air | and creates a little *lift* | for the bird behind it.
By flying in a V, | each goose gets a *boost* | and uses *less* *energy*.
Flying at the *front* of the V | is the *hardest* job of all.
When the *leader* gets *tired*, | it drops *back*, | and another goose moves up | to *take its place*.
All along the way, | the geese keep *honking*.
Scientists *think* | the honking helps the flock *stay together* | and *cheer on* the leader.
In the *spring*, | the geese fly *north* again | to build nests and raise their *goslings*.
So the next time you hear honking *overhead*, | look *up* | and *count* the birds in the V! ↘
Can you *spot* | which goose is the *leader*? ↗
sounds: Have you ever heard loud honking high in the autumn sky? ↗
첫 문장은 듣는 사람에게 진짜 묻듯이 끝을 올려 호기심을 끌어요.
긴 단어는 첫 음절을 크고 길게, 나머지는 약하고 짧게 읽어요.
By flying in a V, each goose gets a boost
이유를 설명하는 문장은 천천히, 핵심어(boost, less energy)를 또렷하게 말해요.
4.expression: Read it like a nature-show host: open with a curious question, explain the science clearly and calmly, and finish with an excited challenge to look up.
